subject: Renewal sequencing: MSA updates + capacity uplift timeline
body:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@starlite.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@starlite.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity uplift request (term change)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Starlite is ready to move forward with the renewal but we need two changes to the paper:

- Increase committed capacity from 1M tokens/mo to 2.5M tokens/mo starting July 1.
- Shift contract term from 12 months to 18 months with an accelerated discount schedule (we want the 12% tier to kick in at 12 months rather than 18).

Procurement asked me to share a clean order form and the current MSA redlines so our legal team can review. Can you confirm timeline for getting a redline back and whether Redwood can accept the proposed billing cadence change (quarterly in arrears -> monthly in arrears)?

Attaching the current Starlite order summary (attached: orderform_v2.pdf).

Best,
Emily
Emily Zhao
Head of Platform
Starlite AI

---

From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@starlite.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2029 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity uplift request (term change)

Hi Emily — great to hear. Thanks for the clear asks. Quick plan from our side: 

1) I’ll get a clean order form (orderform_v3.pdf) to your procurement by EOD tomorrow with the updated capacity and term options reflected as two line items (2.5M committed / 18-month term; and a phased 12-month uplift option as an alternative).

2) Legal: I’ve looped in Lauren (contracts) and Ben (renewal ops). Lauren — can you confirm whether the billing cadence change (monthly in arrears) is acceptable from our side or whether finance needs to preserve quarterly? If we can do monthly we’ll note the change in the order form and mark as approved subject to finance sign-off.

3) Delivery: we need to schedule a quick internal kickoff to lock SLA language and the rollback/fallback policy (in case of capacity burst overage) so your legal gets a single redline set. Suggested internal meeting tomorrow 11:30am PT.

Emily — can you confirm who from Starlite legal should receive the redlines? Procurement was cc’d but if there is a counsel copy please add.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

---

On Fri, 19 Apr 2029 08:20:00 -07:00, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai wrote:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@starlite.ai>, procurement@starlite.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Apr 2029 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity uplift request (term change)

Hannah / Ben — reviewing now. High-level: we can accept the 18-month term and the uplift; redline highlights below and attached.

Key redlines (summary):
- Section 4.2 (Billing cadence): we can move to monthly in arrears but need a clause for minimum invoice amount and a 30-day payment term.
- Section 7.1 (Data residency / logs): Starlite asked for extended log retention; we will agree to 13 months but cannot exceed 18 without SOC2 scope change.
- SLO credits: tightening of latency SLO must not cascade to price credits below existing SLA schedules — propose a one-off service credit schedule for this renewal only.
- Indemnity carveouts: redline narrows the broad indemnity request from Starlite counsel — prefer a mutual indemnity on IP and third-party claims.

I attached a tracked version: redline_msa_trackchanges.docx and a clean order form draft (orderform_v3.pdf).

Action items:
- Hannah: confirm internal meeting 11:30 tomorrow (I’ll bring legal and product).
- Ben: please prepare an impact note for finance on monthly billing (AR cadence + expected collections).
- Emily / procurement: if your counsel has specific alternate language for Section 7 (logs) send as inline comments in the doc or provide a marked up excerpt.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

---

On Fri, 19 Apr 2029 11:32:00 -07:00, ben.carter@redwood.ai wrote:
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@starlite.ai>, procurement@starlite.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Apr 2029 11:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity uplift request (term change)

Quick finance impact: monthly billing is doable but ops prefers 30-day payment term; moving to monthly increases invoicing volume and card/ACH processing fees.

Estimated changes: 
- AR headcount impact: +0.1 FTE (spread across region) for reconciliations at go-live.
- Cashflow: minimal (net new invoicing cadence) — recommend offering a 1% early-pay discount if Starlite signs 18 months and moves to monthly.

I’ll include the cost projections in the internal kickoff. Karthik — product question: for the capacity uplift, is there a preferred phased rollout (e.g., 1.5M for first 3 months then 2.5M) to limit immediate burst usage?

Ben Carter
Director, Renewals Ops
Redwood Inference

---

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@starlite.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@starlite.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Apr 2029 15:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity uplift request (term change)

Thanks all — that schedule works. Procurement asked us to confirm two things before legal review: 
1) Are the SLO credit changes limited to a renewal-specific schedule (we prefer not to renegotiate ongoing SLO credit language)?
2) Can Redwood provide the tracked MSA and a clean order form and a one-page mutual action plan (we uploaded a template here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AStarlite-MAP-2029)

We’ll aim to return comments by EOD Monday. If possible, include a short explainer paragraph in the redline doc summarizing non-standard concessions (billing cadence, credit schedule, retention) to speed review.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Emily

Attachments referenced: orderform_v2.pdf (from Starlite), orderform_v3.pdf (Redwood clean), redline_msa_trackchanges.docx (Redwood tracked)
